Hi Alex — thanks for sending these over. I pulled together a concise summary below; I also attached a lightweight processing map and our subprocessor inventory for the POC scope (see attachments). If you'd like an evidence pack (eg. SOC 2 summary, subproc contracts) we can provide that via a secure GDrive link.

1) Execution locations (where inference executes)
- Hosted POC by default will execute in our US primary region (us-west-2) unless you request EU-only execution.
- For EU-only tenancy we can pin the POC to eu-west-1. Private deployments (VPC/dedicated) can be placed in customer-cloud regions or on-prem.

2) Subprocessors that may handle request/response data during inference pipeline
- Primary compute: Redwood runtime (managed) running on our cloud provider instances (US region for this POC).
- Autoscaling/burst instances: same provider but may be in alternate US zones.
- Observability/metrics: aggregated telemetry (anonymized token-level metrics) is processed by our telemetry backend (subprocessor: Metriclytics Inc., US).
- Storage for logs/artifacts: logs are retained in an encrypted blob store (subprocessor: CloudStoreX, US). See attached CSV for full list and geographic locus per subprocessor.

3) Cross-border hops and data residency notes
- For a US-hosted POC, inference input (prompts) and generated output are processed in the US and do not routinely leave US regions for the inference step.
- If your traffic originates in EU and you choose the default US-hosted POC, requests will cross from EU -> US for execution. We can instead route EU traffic to eu-west-1 to avoid that path.
- Caching (prefix/KV) is regional by default — cache entries for a pinned region remain in that region unless you enable multi-region caching.

4) Retention and deletion relevant to POC
- Short-term retention: request traces and minimal logs for debugging are kept for 30 days by default, then aggregated telemetry retained for 13 months (configurable).
- Customer-controlled data: you can request immediate purge of POC data; we will run a delete workflow which removes active KV entries and schedules blob deletion according to our blob-store's lifecycle (usually within 72 hours for the POC).

If you want, I can scope a single-page evidence summary for procurement and a short diagram showing which subprocessors are in-scope for the POC.

Alex — good follow-ups. I verified details with infra and privacy; responses below with specifics you can send to procurement. I also attached a short SOC2 summary and a secure folder link to subprocessor contracts we can share under an NDA.

1) Subprocessor geography
- Metriclytics Inc.: primary data processing in US-only for telemetry collected as part of the hosted POC. No India/EU processing for telemetry for this POC.
- CloudStoreX: storage operated in the US region tied to the compute tenancy. For EU-tenanted POCs we place blob storage in eu-west-1 and never route blobs out to the US.

2) KV cache persistence
- Default: KV cache is in-memory on the serving instance and kept in RAM-backed storage for low-latency.
- Optional: for customers who enable persistent cache for warm-starts we persist encrypted snapshot files to blob storage in the same region (region-bound backups). Those snapshots are encrypted with customer-scoped keys and follow the retention lifecycle above.

3) Use of raw prompts in analytics
- Short answer: we do not surface raw prompts into long-term analytics in the hosted POC by default.
- Our model-quality pipelines operate on tokenized, metadata-enriched traces where raw PII is redacted; any retention of raw prompts for manual review requires explicit customer opt-in and is governed by a separate data-use agreement.

4) Fallback behaviour and regional routing
- Routing policy for a pinned region: we will not silently route to another region. If eu-west-1 is pinned, requests will queue or failover to a restricted fallback tier only under explicit customer policy (we surface capacity events). We can set a strict no-cross-border-fallback policy for the POC to guarantee execution stays within the pinned region.
